title: Archive every event and announce each one once

blocks.text: Devices upload event ids in batches, and `EventIngest` takes each batch. The raw archive must hold every id the devices sent, repeats included: it is what support reads when a device misbehaves. Subscribers, on the other hand, must hear about each event once, the first time its id arrives, whether the repeat comes in the same batch or a later one.
The previous version did both jobs in a stream and returned the batch size from it. The count was always right; the archive had holes, and subscribers were paged twice for the same door opening.

Write `ingest(batch)` in `src/main/java/practice/EventIngest.java`. It archives every id, announces the new ones, remembers what it has seen, and returns how many ids the batch held. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a batch of new ids is counted and every id in it is announced
every id received reaches the archive, repeats included, in the order received
an id that was already seen, in the same batch or an earlier one, is not announced again

origin.section: A Stream Calls Your Consumer Only for the Elements It Needs, and peek May Not Run at All

concepts: A stream calls peek's Consumer only for the elements its terminal operation pulls: all, one for findFirst, none for count() on a sized source or with no terminal operation, so a required side effect goes in a terminal forEach or a loop.
A lambda or method reference whose expression returns a value, such as seen::add, still compiles as a Consumer and the value is dropped, so a step whose result the caller needs is not a Consumer.
